purpose: Use a genuinely independent EPRL consistent-deformation authority to test whether the published DED and DLD6 two-complexes can be related by the standard amplitude-invariant edge pulling/merging move or a trivial subdivision, without raster geometry, fitted permutations, label tolerances, or post-result equation selection.

deformation.title: On knottings in the physical Hilbert space of LQG as given by the EPRL model
deformation.author: Benjamin Bahr

ded_dld.title: 2-vertex Lorentzian Spin Foam Amplitudes for Dipole Transitions

BAHR: pulling an edge apart changes one edge into two while the number of faces and vertices does not change
the inverse move merges two edges with the same beginning and ending vertices
SARNO: DED denotes the two-vertex one-edge class
DLD denotes the two-vertex two-edge class
the DLD admissible class has one internal face
DLD6 is an explicitly evaluated member of that internal-face class

frozen_invariant_rule: If both authorities are independently qualified, then a Bahr edge split/merge cannot map published DED to DLD because the move preserves the number of faces while the published DLD class contains an internal face absent from the DED one-edge class. Trivial subdivisions are topology/history preserving and are not licensed as deletion or creation of an independent internal-face support.
forbidden: Inferring that no DED-DLD refinement map of any kind exists
Treating this as a failure of EPRL itself
Deleting the DLD internal face by setting j_f=0 post hoc
Using raster thresholds, vector tolerances, fitted permutations, or fitted normalizations
Weakening a source requirement after reading results
